title: Sandwich economics: every public deposit/withdraw is profitable to MEV because slippage is global and not per-call

classification.assetImpact: Recurring value extraction from client funds on every deposit and withdraw via MEV sandwich.
attackPath: 1. The strategy stores a single global slippageTolerance applied to all swaps.
2. Clients have no per-call minOut input and cannot tighten slippage themselves.
3. Every public-facing deposit() or withdraw() emits a Curve swap with predictable, profitable sandwich economics for an MEV searcher.
4. The searcher front-runs to push the pool against the strategy, lets the strategy execute at the worst-allowed price, and back-runs to harvest the imbalance.
5. Loss accrues to the share pool (i.e. all clients pro-rata) on every public call.
classification.likelihood: high - mainnet MEV bots automate this on any public AMM-touching contract
classification.assumptions: deployment on a chain with active MEV (mainnet)

justification: Independent of DEDUP-001's anchor bug, the global static slippage parameter makes every public call structurally MEV-leaky. Direct, recurring theft from client share pools.
